transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been having a hard time with eating at night. It’s a little embarrassing to say. Most nights, after my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen and I eat a lot more than a normal dinner plate—like leftovers, fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls… whatever’s there from an event or the fridge.

Sometimes it gets to where a whole tray is gone, or it feels like half the fridge. I know that probably sounds bad. I just thought I should finally talk to someone about it.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these late-night episodes?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say I’m in control, but honestly, not really. Once I take that first bite, it kind of feels like the decision’s already been made, if that makes sense.

I’ll be telling myself, “George, stop now, you don’t need more,” but my hands are already fixing another plate or opening another container. It’s embarrassing to admit, but that’s usually how it goes.
Do you usually feel guilty after these late-night eating episodes?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try not to make too big a thing of it, because I know people have worse problems, but afterward I feel pretty awful about myself.

It’s like… people see me as this organized, strong guy who has things handled, and then there I am sitting there feeling ashamed and guilty, kind of disgusted with myself that I let it happen again. I don’t know if that’s the right way to say it, but… yeah, I feel sick with myself afterward.
Do you feel like you're eating really quickly during these late-night episodes?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but during those times I eat really fast.

Sometimes I barely even taste it, which is kind of sad because it might be food I normally enjoy or used to take pride in cooking. I’ll be standing at the counter taking these big bites, and I’m swallowing before I’ve really finished chewing the last one. It’s not… it’s not how I’d normally want to eat.
Are you usually feeling stressed, anxious, or upset right before these late-night eating episodes?

I’m… not totally sure, to be honest. I haven’t really tracked it closely enough to say, “yes, it’s always stress” or anything like that.

Sometimes I only realize afterward that I was wound up or bothered by something, but in the moment it’s more like I just end up in the kitchen and don’t think it through. I don’t know if that answers it the right way.
Do you ever feel like you're not really aware of what you're doing while you're eating at night?

Yeah… I guess that does happen. I mean, I’m not completely blacked out or anything, I know I’m in the kitchen, but it’s like once I take that first bite, something shifts.

I’ll be telling myself, “George, stop now, you don’t need more,” but my hands are already fixing another plate or opening another container. It feels like the decision’s kind of been made already, if that makes sense. Like I’m there, but I’m not really… in charge of it the way I should be.
Do you think you're eating an amount of food that's significantly more than what most people would eat in one sitting during these episodes?

Yeah… I think I’d have to say yes. I don’t like admitting that, because it sounds really bad, but it’s more than just having seconds or a late snack.

Most nights, after my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen and it can be… a lot. Like not just one plate. I’ll start with leftovers—fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls, things like that—and then I keep going way past what I think most people would eat at one sitting. Sometimes it’s like a whole tray is gone, or it feels like I’ve cleared out half the fridge.

I know that probably sounds excessive. I’m not trying to make excuses for it. It just kind of keeps going once I start.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these episodes?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I have no responsibility at all, because I know I’m the one doing it.

But once I take that first bite, it really does feel like the decision’s already been made somehow. I’ll be thinking, George, stop now, that’s enough, and at the same time my hands are already fixing another plate or opening another container.

So… yes, I guess I do feel unable to stop, at least in those moments. Is that what you mean?
How often do these late-night eating episodes happen?

Um… more often than I’d like to admit, honestly.

I was hoping it was just kind of an occasional thing, but if I’m being straight with you, it’s been going on for months now. I can’t really think of a week where it didn’t happen at least once. And… most weeks, it’s several nights, usually after my wife has gone to bed.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of answer you’re looking for, but that’s probably the honest one.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during these episodes because you feel an intense urge to continue eating?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair to say.

I don’t want to overstate it, but in the moment it feels like this really strong pull to keep going. Once I take that first bite, it’s almost like the decision’s already been made for me. I’ll be thinking, George, stop now, that’s enough, and somehow my hands are still fixing another plate or opening another container.

I know that sounds kind of bad. But yes… it does feel like I’m not really controlling how much I’m eating once it starts.
Do these late-night eating episodes usually happen when you're feeling emotionally upset or distressed?

I’m not totally sure, honestly.

I mean, sometimes I can tell I’m tense or in a bad mood beforehand, but I haven’t really tracked it closely enough to say that’s usually why it happens. It’s more like… by the time I realize what I’m doing, I’m already in the kitchen.

Sorry, is that too vague? I just don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.
Do you feel like you're unable to control what you're eating during these episodes because you feel like you're in a trance-like state or disconnected from your actions?

I don’t know if I’d call it a trance exactly… that sounds a little dramatic, maybe.

But there is this disconnected feeling, I guess. Like once I take the first bite, it feels like the decision’s already kind of been made, and even while I’m telling myself, “George, stop now,” my hands are still getting more food or opening something else.

So… yes, maybe not a trance in the movie sense, but I don’t feel fully in control of what I’m doing.
Do you feel like these late-night eating episodes are causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make it sound worse than it is, but yes. It bothers me a lot afterward.

In the moment I kind of push everything aside, but once it’s over, I just feel… sick with myself. Like people see me as this organized, solid guy, someone who has things under control, and then I’m sitting there feeling ashamed and guilty and honestly pretty disgusted that I let it happen again.

Sorry, I don’t know if that’s the kind of answer you mean, but yes, it’s distressing.
Do you feel like you're unable to control what you're eating during these episodes because you feel like something is taking over?

I guess “something taking over” is close… I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not responsible, because I know it’s still me doing it.

But once I take that first bite, it really does feel like the decision’s already been made somehow. Even while I’m thinking, “George, stop now,” my hands are still fixing another plate or opening another container.

So… yes, in that sense, it feels like I’m not really the one steering anymore.
Have you had these late-night eating episodes every week for the past few months?

Yeah… I think so. I wish I could say there were weeks I skipped, but for months now I honestly can’t think of a single week where it didn’t happen at least once.

And, um… most weeks it’s more than once. Usually several nights, after my wife has gone to bed. I’m not proud of that, but yes, weekly for sure.
Do you ever find that after one of these late-night eating episodes, you don't really remember what you ate?

I don’t think so… not like a blackout or anything. I usually have at least a pretty good idea of what I ate.

Sometimes the next morning I’ll see wrappers or dishes and it sort of hits me more clearly, like, “Oh, right, I had that too.” But I wouldn’t say I completely don’t remember. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever find yourself wondering the next morning what you had eaten during one of these episodes?

Sometimes, yeah, but not in a total blank way. It’s more like I wake up and think, “Wait… did I also eat that?” and then I’ll see something in the trash or a plate and remember.

I don’t want to overstate it—I’m not completely unaware of what happened. It’s just… the amount or the exact stuff can be a little fuzzy until I’m reminded, if that makes sense.
